stories.headline: 2026 NBA buzz: Latest free agency and trade updates
stories.summary: We're tracking deals, trades and buzz across the NBA, including Steph Curry's new extension with the Warriors.
stories.body:
NBA free agency has almost reached the end, with several players landing in new homes this offseason.

LeBron James decided to continue his historic career with the Philadelphia 76ers after months of deliberation. The Sixers also traded for Jaylen Brown this summer, turning the franchise into a true contender with two huge moves.

Meanwhile, Giannis Antetokounmpo is headed to South Beach to team up with Bam Adebayo and the Miami Heat, and the Los Angeles Lakers have been sold for the second time in 10 months.

What will happen next during this turbulent offseason?

Check back here for all the latest buzz, news and reactions from our ESPN NBA insiders, with the latest info at the top:

Quick links:

Free agency grades | Trade grades

Trade tracker | Transactions

Depth charts | Trade machine | More

Sept. 25

What's next for Curry and the Warriors?

Stephen Curry's two-year, $116 million extension has put the Golden State Warriors in a position to have spending power next summer.

By Curry taking $10 million less than the maximum allowed, the Warriors project to have nearly $38 million in cap space in 2027. Golden State could increase their projection to $55 million if center Kristaps Porzingis is waived in the offseason. Porzingis' $20 million salary for next season is guaranteed for only $3 million.

For Golden State to have ample room, forwards Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III would need to sign elsewhere or at a significantly lesser salary. Both players are free agents next summer.

Both salary projections include the $17 million free agent hold of guard Brandin Podziemski. The former first-round pick is eligible up until Oct. 19 to extend his contract. -- Bobby Marks

Grizzlies waive D'Angelo Russell

The Memphis Grizzlies have wavied D'Angelo Russell, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Russell has made one All-Star team during his career and was selected No. 2 in the 2015 NBA draft.

Sept. 23

Sources: Status of Mavs big man Lively up in air
Dallas Mavericks center Dereck Lively II has not been cleared for training camp and his status for the start of the regular season has yet to be determined as he continues to recover from right foot surgery, sources told ESPN's Tim MacMahon.

After playing a key role as a rookie in the Mavericks' run to the 2024 NBA Finals, Lively's promising career has been derailed by recurring problems with his right foot, which has been surgically repaired twice in the last 14 months.

Lively is ramping up toward being cleared for basketball activity, sources said, emphasizing that the team is not discouraged by his progress. Dallas begins training camp on Saturday.

Extension unlikely as Knicks, Towns talks stall
Talks have stagnated between the New York Knicks and Karl-Anthony Towns on a contract extension, and an agreement is considered unlikely as the team begins training camp next week, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania and Vincent Goodwill on Wednesday.

The sides have spent extensive time discussing a potential extension during the offseason, but there has been no movement lately in negotiations, sources said, as the Knicks stand to go for a repeat following their first NBA title in 53 years.

Sept. 22

Charania: Hield, Nembhard to Charlotte for Finney-Smith
The Atlanta Hawks are trading Dorian Finney-Smith to the Charlotte Hornets for Buddy Hield, Ryan Nembhard and cash, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Leonard, Raptors agree to two-year extension
The Toronto Raptors and Kawhi Leonard have agreed to a two-year, $115 million extension, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Leonard now has a total of three years and $165 million left on his deal.

The 2026-27 season will be Leonard's first back in Toronto since the 2018-19 campaign, a season in which he helped lead the Raptors to their only title in franchise history.

Sept. 21

Charania: Pistons, Duren at an "impasse"
Free agent center Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons are at an impasse this season and the franchise is uncertain if he will show up to next Monday's Media Day, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

"When you talk to people close to [Duren], he feels a certain way toward the Pistons' respect level for him," Charania said on NBA Today. "For him it's been all about respect, for the team it has just been about business. ... Over the course of this offseason, his offer has been been around the $180 to $190 million over five years range. And that has also included incentives like weight clauses to my understanding. And that has all played a part in this as well.

"Over the last several weeks it's kind of quiet on this front. The sides have picked up communication. And I am told right now the Pistons offer to Jalen Duren is $200 million over five years."

Duren has until Oct. 1 to sign a qualifying offer.

Hawks' Henri Veesaar out with torn ACL

The Atlanta Hawks announced that center Henri Veesaar tore his ACL during a Sept. 15 workout. He will undergo surgery in October and is expected to miss the entire 2026-27 season.

Sept. 18

Pistons, Thompson reach five-year, $155 million extension
Detroit Pistons All-Defensive forward Ausar Thompson has agreed to a five-year, $155 million rookie-scale contract extension with the franchise, sources told ESPN.

Thompson lands the fully guaranteed extension after making first-team All-Defense and finishing third in Defensive Player of the Year voting last season. The 23-year-old averaged 9.9 points, 5.7 rebounds, 3.1 assists and 0.9 blocks in 2025-26 while leading the NBA in steals per game (2.0).

Heat, Larsson agree to four-year, $60 million extension
Miami Heat guard Pelle Larsson has agreed to a new four-year, $60 million contract extension, with a mutual option for the 2030-31 season, Austin Brown and Steven Heumann of CAA Sports told ESPN on Friday.

A second-round find in the 2024 draft, the 6-foot-5 guard avoids restricted free agency next summer and locks in a new deal with a mutual option that fully guarantees $60 million while allowing either side to opt in on 2030.

Jazz, George agree on a five-year, rookie-scale extension
Utah Jazz guard Keyonte George have agreed on a five-year, $157.5 million rookie-scale contract extension with the franchise, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania and Tim MacMahon. George was the No. 16 pick in the 2023 draft and has averaged 17.2 points and 5.3 assists per game in his three seasons with the Jazz.

Sept. 17

Bey, Pelicans agree to three-year extension
New Orleans Pelicans' Saddiq Bey agreed to a three-year, $55.5 million contract extension with the franchise, plus a trade kicker, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Bey averaged a career-high 17.7 points per game last season after missing all of the 2024-25 season with a torn ACL.

Sept. 16

Kings remain interested in Duren
The Sacramento Kings continue to loom in the background of Jalen Duren's restricted free agency with the incumbent Detroit Pistons.

Kings general manager Scott Perry met with Duren for dinner in Miami in early July and has maintained a level of steady interest in the ultimate outcome of Duren's free agency, though a path to acquire Duren this summer remains blocked.

The Pistons declined any legitimate conversation about a Duren sign-and-trade to the Kings for starting center Domantas Sabonis and have maintained a strong stance about their intention to keep Duren.

As ESPN reported earlier this month, the Pistons have a five-year offer in the $35 million per year range on the table, but that hasn't been enough to entice the disgruntled Duren to sign.

His greatest piece of leverage is a risky one -- the $9.6 million qualifying offer that would make him an unrestricted free agent next summer, when Sacramento will have flexibility for the first time in Perry's tenure as general manager. Zach LaVine's $48.9 million contract and De'Andre Hunter's $24.9 million contract both expire, allowing the Kings to generate a max offer for Duren, should he be available.

But that would only be the case if Duren is willing to take a massive one-year paycut and accept the risk of the qualifying offer. Until then, the Kings remain in the background as an interested long-term suitor helping Duren's leverage. -- Anthony Slater

Knicks sign Brown to training camp contract
The New York Knicks are signing Bruce Brown to a training camp contract, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. New York will also have "John Konchar, Drew Eubanks and others enter camp to compete for the final regular season roster," per Charania.

Sept. 15

Shams: NBA Las Vegas expansion plans due Thursday
The NBA and commissioner Adam Silver are in deep expansion conversations with Las Vegas, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania, with the next round of bids due Thursday. Charania also reported that the final round of bids will be due shortly after this round and that his understanding is that the Las Vegas expansion proposal could exceed $10 billion.

The expansion process is ongoing in Seattle as well, per Charania, but hasn't gained as much momentum as Las Vegas currently. Charania expects clarity on votes on both expansion franchises "over the next couple months."

Sept. 14

Sources: Duren feels 'disrespected' in contract talks
The Detroit Pistons are focused on bringing back restricted free agent Jalen Duren, Andscape's Marc Spears said on "NBA Today," but there are feelings to mend.

"They have some optimism, but it's complicated," Spears said. "I just hear that, for Jalen, it's not about money right now. He feels disrespected. ... There's a black cloud going into camp. ... They gotta try to fix it, and I don't know if they can in time."

Kawhi Leonard trade to Toronto officially confirmed

The trade sending Kawhi Leonard to the Toronto Raptors for Gradey Dick, Brandon Ingram and future draft picks was confirmed Monday, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Taj Gibson officially retires, joins Bulls as assistant coach

Following a 17-year NBA career, Taj Gibson has retired and agreed to return to the Chicago Bulls as an assistant coach under Tiago Splitter, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Sept. 13

Ballmer and Clippers to comply with NBA punishments
Eleven days after the NBA issued punishments stemming from its investigation into the LA Clippers' dealings with Kawhi Leonard, team owner Steve Ballmer issued a statement saying he and the team would comply with them.

Those punishments include a $30 million fine, yearlong suspensions for Ballmer and president of business operations Gillian Zucker, a six-month suspension for president of basketball operations Lawrence Frank, and five lost first-round picks.

Sept. 10

Justice Department opens criminal inquiry into Clippers' dealings with Leonard
The U.S. Justice Department has opened a criminal investigation into the LA Clippers, The New York Times reported Thursday evening, looking at how the team allegedly arranged secret sponsorship contracts for Leonard.

The probe is being conducted by the U.S. attorney's office in Brooklyn, New York.

Sept. 8

Pelicans trade Hawkins to Grizzlies in four-player deal
The New Orleans Pelicans have traded Jordan Hawkins, Micah Peavy, a future second-round pick and a future second-round pick swap to the Memphis Grizzlies for AJ Johnson and Taj Gibson, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Tuesday.

The trade clears roster space for the Pelicans, frees up salary flexibility to sign Bennedict Mathurin to a two-year, $16 million deal, and allows the team to have a look at a young player in Johnson, who was the No. 21 pick in the 2023 NBA draft. Hawkins, a lottery pick at No. 14 in the same draft, now gets dealt by his team prior to his fourth season.

Sept. 4

Ben Simmons signs with Kings on one-year deal
Three-time All-Star Ben Simmons has agreed to a one-year, $3.5 million deal with the Sacramento Kings, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. The deal marks a return to the NBA for Simmons, who sat out the 2025-26 season. Simmons was the No. 1 pick in the 2016 NBA draft.

Sept. 3

Windhorst: Steve Ballmer 'very' angry after NBA penalty
ESPN's Brian Windhorst reported that LA Clippers owner Steve Ballmer is 'very angry' after the penalties handed down to the franchise by the NBA on Sept. 2.

"When you're worth $150 billion and you're angry, and he's very clearly angry, you can't advise him, you can't talk to him," Windhorst said on Get Up. "I'd be stunned if his lawyers didn't advise him, as Shams [Charania] said, to make a plea deal because he should've made a please deal."

Read more: NBA punishes Clippers after Kawhi investigation: Top questions​

Thompson, Rockets agree to five-year contract extension
The Houston Rockets and Amen Thompson have agreed to a five-year, $208 million rookie-scale contract extension, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania The deal includes a 10% trade kicker.

Sept. 2

NBA insiders answer the biggest questions on NBA's Clippers investigation
After the NBA released the findings of its yearlong investigation into allegations that the LA Clippers circumvented the salary cap in order to funnel money to Kawhi Leonard, ESPN NBA insiders Baxter Holmes, Brian Windhorst, Ramona Shelburne and Bobby Marks examined the report, the massive punishments the NBA leveled and how all of it could impact this season -- and beyond.

The punishment was compounded by the Clippers being previous offenders during Steve Ballmer's tenure as owner. They were fined $250,000 for a similar accusation involving DeAndre Jordan in 2015. There also was a 2019 investigation into Leonard's signing in which the Clippers were cleared of wrongdoing but subsequently warned and put through a seminar to remind them of the rules.
This penalty is indeed harsh, but it could have been worse.

In the case of Joe Smith and the Minnesota Timberwolves in 2000, his contract was voided and his Bird rights were vacated.

Leonard will have to write a sizable check -- $700,000 -- but he will not be suspended, and his contract and Bird rights remain unaffected.

The Clippers and the Toronto Raptors will be allowed to move forward in their trade process, one league source said. If the trade moves forward, LA will acquire two first-round picks in the deal. -- Windhorst

Read the full story here.

Charania: NBA rules on Kawhi Leonard-Aspiration investigation
Sources told ESPN's Shams Charania reported that, after a year-long probe into Kawhi Leonard-Aspiration connection, the NBA has stripped the LA Clippers of five first-round picks and issued a $30 million fine to owner Steve Ballmer, as well as suspended Ballmer, Lawrence Frank and Gillian Zucker.

On top of that, Leonard will have to pay $700,000 in restitution for improper benefits by the franchise for his uncle and former business representative, Dennis Robertson. Leonard will not be suspended but Robertson is banned by the NBA from all business dealings.

SEC requesting information from Daktronics regarding Clippers probe
The Securities and Exchange Commission is seeking information from Daktronics, the company that designed the LA Clippers' videoboard inside the Intuit Dome, related to Kawhi Leonard, a company executive said Wednesday.

"Let me now briefly address a matter that has been in the media concerning the NBA's investigation of Kawhi Leonard and the Clippers in connection with the league's collective bargaining agreement that many of you may have heard about," chief financial officer Howard Atkins said on Daktronics' quarterly earnings call.

"As you might expect, we have received requests for information from the NBA. Additionally, the Securities and Exchange Commission is seeking information from us concerning the company and Mr. Leonard. "We take these requests seriously and are cooperating. At this point, out of respect for the respective processes, we will not be providing further comment."

A spokesperson for the SEC declined to comment.

Podcaster Pablo Torre reported last month that Daktronics had an undisclosed sponsorship agreement allegedly worth millions of dollars with Leonard.

Torre interviewed someone identified as an "anonymous high-level source under contract for Intuit Dome" who alleged that the sponsorship deal "was 1,000% a way to circumvent the salary cap. It was funneling money from the Clippers through Daktronics back to Kawhi."

The NBA launched its investigation into the Clippers and Leonard last September after numerous podcasts from Torre, who cited internal documents that showed that Clippers owner Steve Ballmer invested $50 million in Aspiration, a now-defunct green banking company, through his personal LLC in September 2021.

That month, the Clippers signed a 23-year, $300 million deal with Aspiration, making the company the "first founding partner" of the Intuit Dome.

Six months later, Aspiration signed its $28 million endorsement deal with Leonard.

An unnamed employee who purportedly worked for the banking company told Torre that Leonard's sponsorship deal "was to circumvent the salary cap."

The Clippers have repeatedly denied that they funneled money through Aspiration to compensate Leonard.

On Aug. 17, ESPN reported that the NBA has found no evidence showing Ballmer funneled money through team sponsors to pay Leonard in order to circumvent the salary cap, per three people with knowledge of recent discussions between the two sides. -- Baxter Holmes

Sept. 1

Windhorst: Sabonis hired new agent this summer, could want out of Sacramento

On the Sept. 1 episode of "The Hoop Collective," ESPN's Brian Windhorst discussed what Domantas Sabonis hiring a new agent this summer could mean for his future with the Sacramento Kings.

Windhorst on Sabonis hiring a new agent: " I do think it's somewhat interesting that he changed agents this offseason. He hired Aaron Mintz of CAA. Steve Heumann and that group. One of the top executives at CAA. This last year, Mintz and his group executed the trade for Trae Young away from Atlanta, executed the trade for Walker Kessler away from the [Jazz]. Domantas Sabonis just hired him.

"At the risk of ... parodying myself from the season, why would he do that?"

Aug. 29

Latest on Curry's next deal decision

The window for Stephen Curry to sign an extension has officially opened.

The four-time champion and two-time MVP is now eligible (through June 30) to sign a two-year, $136.7 million extension. If he signs, Curry will become the first player in NBA history to rack up more than $600 million in on-court earnings.

A new contract for Curry will have important financial implications for Golden State. With Curry, Draymond Green and Jimmy Butler III able to become free agents after the 2026-27 season, Golden State could have significant cap space to reshape its roster.

If Curry signs for the maximum allowed in the first season of an extension ($65.7 million), the Warriors project to have between $45 million and $60 million in cap space next offseason. -- Bobby Marks

Wolves, Jazz swap forwards
The Minnesota Timberwolves are trading forward Josh Green to the Utah Jazz for forwards Cody Williams and John Konchar, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

The Wolves are expected to keep Williams, the No. 10 pick in 2024, and waive-and-stretch Konchar, sources said. By moving Green's $14.7 million salary, Minnesota can sign Jonathan Kuminga to the taxpayer midlevel exception.

Aug. 27

Free agent center Richards agrees to one-year deal with Heat
Free agent center Nick Richards has agreed to a one-year deal with the Miami Heat, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. After signing Klay Thompson, the Heat fill roster slot No. 14 with a reserve big man.

Aug. 26

Kuminga signs two-year deal with Minnesota
Free agent forward Jonathan Kuminga agreed to a two-year, $12.4 million deal with the Minnesota Timberwolves, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. Kuminga probably will start alongside Anthony Edwards, LaMelo Ball, Jaden McDaniels and Rudy Gobert.

Mathurin to sign with Pels
Free agent guard Bennedict Mathurin agreed to a two-year, $16 million deal with the New Orleans Pelicans, including a player option, sources tell ESPN.

Aug. 25

Warriors agree to deal with Niang

Forward Georges Niang agreed to a one-year, $3.9 million deal with the Golden State Warriors, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Warriors sign guard Williams
Free agent guard Brandon Williams is signing a one-year, $2.6M deal with the Golden State Warriors, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Williams averaged 13 points and 3.9 assists per game last season for the Dallas Mavericks.

Aug. 24

Blazers lose Sharpe to injury
Portland Trail Blazers guard Shaedon Sharpe sustained a torn meniscus in his right knee, and he is expected to miss six months, sources told ESPN.

Sharpe, 23, averaged 20.8 points for the Blazers last season but missed a large chunk of the campaign with a stress fracture of his left fibula.

His four-year, $90 million extension, which he signed last year, officially kicks in this season. Sharpe will make $20.1 million in 2026-27.

Aug. 21

Nuggets signing DeRozan to one-year deal
Six-time NBA All-Star DeMar DeRozan agreed to sign with the Denver Nuggets on a one-year, $3.9 million deal, sources told ESPN on Friday.

DeRozan landed on the Nuggets after speaking to the Miami Heat, Washington Wizards and New Orleans Pelicans during free agency, choosing a significant role in Denver and a chance to compete in the West. The Nuggets' front office and coaches made a strong recruitment effort in recent weeks to secure DeRozan's commitment, showing him how he would complement Nikola Jokic and Jamal Murray as an additional playmaker. He also gives the Nuggets a veteran backcourt presence after sending young, versatile wing Peyton Watson to Cleveland as part of a four-team trade.

Mavs buy out Thompson, to sign with Heat
Klay Thompson is expected to sign with the Miami Heat after clearing waivers following his contract buyout from the Dallas Mavericks, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Friday.

Thompson, 36, was due to make $17.5 million in the final season of his contract with the Mavericks, who announced his buyout Friday afternoon.

He played two seasons for the Mavericks, averaging 12.9 points per game and shooting 38.7% from 3-point range. Thompson passed Damian Lillard last season to rank fourth in career 3-pointers made.

Aug. 20

Harden to return to Cavs
Free agent James Harden agreed to sign a three-year, $97M contract to return to the Cleveland Cavaliers, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania, with a player option for the 2028-29 season.

The Cavs acquired Harden, who turns 37 on Aug. 26, from the LA Clippers in early February in a trade for guard Darius Garland. Cleveland went 21-9 after Harden debuted, tied for the fifth-best record after Feb. 7, as he averaged 20.5 points, 7.7 assists and 4.8 rebounds per game after the All-Star break.

Aug. 19

Watson to Cavs in multiteam trade
The Cleveland Cavaliers, Denver Nuggets and LA Clippers agreed on a trade sending Peyton Watson to the Cavaliers, Max Strus to LA, and an unprotected 2031 Cavs first-round pick and 2032 Sacramento Kings second-rounder to the Nuggets, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania. As part of the trade, the Cavaliers will send Tre Mann to the Washington Wizards for Cam Whitmore and a 2027 second-round pick.

Watson will sign a new four-year, $88 million deal with Cleveland.

Aug. 17

Suns, Highsmith agree to one-year deal

The Phoenix Suns and forward Haywood Highsmith agreed to a one-year deal, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Watford, Pelicans agree to one-year deal
Free agent forward Trendon Watford agreed to a one-year, $2.9 million deal with the New Orleans Pelicans, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Watford, 25, considered multiple options, but for New Orleans he serves as a productive two-way get late into the offseason.

Aug. 14

Cavaliers trade Schroder, cash to Hornets for Mann
The Cleveland Cavaliers are trading Dennis Schroder and cash to the Charlotte Hornets for Tre Mann, sources told ESPN on Friday.

The Hornets, Cavaliers and Schroder's rep, Mark Bartelstein of Priority Sports, worked for the past couple months on the deal, which also provides Cleveland flexibility to continue pursuing roster moves and tax savings to keep the team well under the second apron, according to ESPN's Bobby Marks.

Aug. 13

Beal re-signs with Clippers
Free agent guard Bradley Beal agreed to a two-year, $13.2 million deal to return to the LA Clippers, with a player option in the second season, Mark Bartelstein of Priority Sports told ESPN.

After declining his $5.6 million player option, Beal sifted through options over the last month in free agency, including interest from the Miami Heat, before landing on the Clippers. He returns to LA after rehabbing from hip surgery that cost him all but six games last season.

Aug. 12
Westbrook announces retirement from NBA
Russell Westbrook, the 2017 MVP, a nine-time All-NBA selection and the league's all-time triple-double leader, is retiring from the NBA, the 37-year-old announced on Wednesday. Westbrook had contract offers this offseason from the Sacramento Kings and Washington Wizards but chose to step away on his own terms, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Drafted No. 4 overall by the Seattle SuperSonics in 2008 just before the franchise relocated to Oklahoma City, Westbrook played 11 of his 18 seasons with the Thunder. The electric guard and Hall of Fame lock then spent the remainder of his career with the Houston Rockets, Wizards, Los Angeles Lakers, LA Clippers, Denver Nuggets and Kings.

Westbrook retires with the fifth most assists in NBA history (10,351).

NBA world praises 'legendary' career

Aug. 11

McMenamin: NBA excited to grow product with 3 p.m. opening day tip-off
ESPN's Dave McMenamin went on NBA Today to discuss the recent schedule release for the NBA's opening day and Christmas games.

"I've talked to people around the league today and they're like we could sense the excitement for the NBA right now. So let's experiment with this thing," McMenamin said. "They talked with executives at NBC, and it was kind of a joint decision that this is something we can turn into a celebration of the game. It's already a marquee moment for the league. Let's see if we can enhance it and turn it into a major showcase. Maybe down the line, this becomes a tradition for NBA fans. ... [Also the NBA is] an international game. 3 p.m. Eastern is primetime viewing in Europe."

The Boston Celtics and Detroit Pistons open the season on Tuesday, Oct. 20 at 3 p.m. ET on NBA/Peacock.

What's latest on Kawhi and the Clippers? And updates on Nuggets, Suns
Brian is joined by ESPN's Anthony Slater to discuss the latest in the ongoing Kawhi Leonard-LA Clippers situation, including how it could impact the Toronto Raptors and the Eastern Conference during the 2026-27 season. They move on to the cover the Dillon Brooks' contract and how it impacts the future spending plans for the Phoenix Suns. The duo then closes on how the Denver Nuggets' books put them in trouble moving forward, and a remembrance of Don Nelson.

Windhorst on the newest Kawhi Leonard situation: "That's obviously key: Did he get money from Daktronics? Slater, if this is accurate, the Clippers side of it is devastating.
But let's put that aside for right now. For the actual business of the NBA for the 26-27 season, this is not just a Clipper issue. Last year was a Clipper issue. Now, it is no longer just a Clipper issue. Whether Kahwi Leonard is on the Raptors or not has a huge circumstantial fallout in the Eastern Conference and then obviously like you know DeMar DeRozan is held up to a certain extent, for example. James Harden is hasn't done his business with the Cavs because they're waiting on things.

Latest episodes of the 'Hoop Collective' podcast

Aug. 7

NBA insiders: Updates on the biggest remaining NBA free agents

ESPN's NBA insiders came together to give updates on the top remaining free agents this season. Highlights include:

Multiple teams are pursuing Peyton Watson, including the Atlanta Hawks, LA Clippers, Milwaukee Bucks and Cleveland Cavaliers
The Detroit Pistons remain the favorite to sign Jalen Duren but the two sides are at an impasse
The Los Angeles Lakers are interested Jonathan Kuminga
James Harden is on track for a multi-year deal with Cleveland
DeMar DeRozan has drawn interest from the Miami Heat, Denver Nuggets, Washington Wizards and Cavaliers

Read more: Updates on the biggest remaining NBA free agents

Aug. 5

Brooks, Suns agree to three-year, $73 million extension
Phoenix Suns forward Dillon Brooks agreed Wednesday to a three-year, $73 million contract extension through 2029-30, agent Mike George of Klutch Sports told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Credited with helping to establish a new culture in Phoenix, Brooks is coming off the best season of his nine-year career. He averaged a career-high 20.2 points to go with 3.6 rebounds and 1.8 assists for a surprise 45-win playoff team that maintained continuity throughout the offseason. In addition to bringing back Brooks, the Suns signed Collin Gillespie, Mark Williams and Jordan Goodwin to multiyear contracts and also acquired Miles Bridges and Luke Kennard.

Slater: Kings were actively shopping Sabonis at deadline, draft
ESPN's Anthony Slater reported that the Sacramento Kings were openly shopping forward Domantas Sabonis at the trade deadline and the 2026 draft.

The Kings nearly traded Sabonis to the Toronto Raptors at the deadline in February -- a move he would've welcomed, a source with knowledge of the situation said -- for a package that included RJ Barrett, but the Raptors were unable to get off the three-year, $84 million remaining on Jakob Poeltl's contract, which doomed the deal.
Sabonis had season-ending surgery on a partially torn meniscus later that month, and the Kings revisited trade talks surrounding him this summer. Perry visited with restricted free agent center Jalen Duren in early July and explored the idea of a sign-and-trade swap of big men, but the Detroit Pistons balked at the idea of losing Duren for Sabonis, league sources said.

There were predraft conversations about Sabonis with the Charlotte Hornets (who held pick Nos. 14 and 18) and at least one phone call with the Boston Celtics, team and league sources said, but nothing materialized. In Charlotte's case, the idea would've been to pair Sabonis with point guard LaMelo Ball, but the franchise instead opted to trade Ball for draft picks and lean further into a youth movement.

Read more: Darius Acuff is the Kings' future, but they still have to manage the present

July 30

Shelburne: The Cavaliers are still poking around with Peyton Watson
Appearing on ESPN's "NBA Today," Ramona Shelburne gave the latest on James Harden's free agency status after the All-Star declined a $42.3 million player option. "The Cavs are still poking around with Peyton Watson and I think that's why James has given them a lot of room to negotiate."

Shelburne: The Raptors have given zero indication of backing out of the Leonard trade
Ramona Shelburne appeared on ESPN's "NBA Today" to weigh in on the pending Aspiration investigation after Baxter Holmes reported today that the case could drag into 2027. "I haven't heard [the Raptors] trying to back out. I think the discussion is more of a leaguewide discussion."

July 28

76ers trade Broome, pick to Clippers for cash considerations
The Philadelphia 76ers are trading Johni Broome and a second-round pick to the LA Clippers for cash considerations, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Shams: Nuggets tweak asking price for potential Watson trade

Appearing on ESPN's "NBA Today," Shams Charania reported that the Denver Nuggets have lowered their asking price in a potential sign-and-trade of restricted free agent wing Peyton Watson. "The Nuggets initially had set a price this offseason of -- similar to the Walker Kessler deal -- two firsts and two swaps," Charania said. "Now that price is a really good high-level player as well as a first-round pick."

Shams: Wizards looking to add another scorer?

Appearing on ESPN's "NBA Today," Shams Charania reported that the Washington Wizards have had conversations with free agent guard DeMar DeRozan in recent days. The Wizards join the Miami Heat, Denver Nuggets and Cleveland Cavaliers among franchises to show interest in the six-time All-Star. DeRozan, who will turn 37 in August, was waived by the Sacramento Kings on July 6.

Warriors, Green agree to one-year deal

Draymond Green has agreed to return to the Golden State Warriors on a one-year, $27.7 million deal, Klutch Sports CEO Rich Paul told ESPN's Shams Charania.

Green turned down his $27.6 million player option earlier this summer in a surprising move shortly before free agency kicked off. The decision created financial flexibility for Golden State, which was among the teams in the running to land LeBron James.

However, after James eventually decided to take his talents to Philadelphia, Green and the Warriors moved forward on a new deal.

Will Towns get the max from Knicks?

Appearing on ESPN's "First Take," Brian Windhorst explained why the New York Knicks might hesitate on giving Karl-Anthony Towns a maximum contract extension of four years at $272 million.

"He's extension-eligible now. They could do this deal today. They haven't done the deal. They don't have an agreement on it. KAT is coming off the highest achievement of his career. Why Dolan is so worried about the second apron
The New York Knicks' championship parade has not even started, but there are already questions over whether finances will break up the roster.

"If we could bring back the whole team, exactly as is, why wouldn't you?" Knicks owner James Dolan said Wednesday on WFAN's "Carton Show." "I don't know if we'll be able to.

"We're willing to stretch, but there's certain things in the NBA that you'd have to be suicidal to do. One of them is the second apron. Cannot go into the second apron."

Including the 24th pick in next week's draft (June 23 and 24, 8 p.m. ET on ABC/ESPN), New York is $13 million below the second apron and has decisions with free agents Landry Shamet, Mitchell Robinson and possibly Jose Alvarado. (Alvarado has until Monday to decide on his $4.5 million option.) The entire starting five, meanwhile, is under contract through at least 2026-27. Karl-Anthony Towns is extension-eligible this summer and can become a free agent in the 2027 offseason if an agreement is not reached.

The second apron is a punitive luxury tax threshold restricting how teams add to their rosters in free agency, trades and the draft. In the case of the Knicks, the team would not be allowed to send cash in a trade, use the $6.1 million tax midlevel exception, aggregate salaries in a trade or use more than 100% of the traded player exception.

A team cannot trade its first-round pick seven years out if it finishes over the second apron in consecutive seasons, which no team has ever done. That same pick could be moved back to the end of the first round if a team finishes over the second apron in three out of four seasons. Luckily for Dolan and the Knicks, there are no rules that prohibit a team from retaining its own players.

New York can exceed the threshold to sign Robinson, Shamet and Alvarado. If the Knicks let the three players sign elsewhere, they would have their first-round pick (New York also has the 31st and 55th picks in the second round), the $6.1 million tax midlevel exception and $2.5 million veteran minimum exceptions available as replacements.

Since the apron rules were implemented before the 2024-25 season, Cleveland, Phoenix, Minnesota and Boston have finished the regular season over the second apron. The Knicks finished the past two seasons $53,000 and $370,000 below. Next offseason, New York is projected to be $31 million below the second apron with seven players under contract. -- Bobby Marks

Why LaMelo's flagrant 2 falls into a gray area
The NBA retroactively assessed Charlotte Hornets guard LaMelo Ball with a flagrant foul 2 for tripping Miami Heat center Bam Adebayo in Tuesday's Eastern Conference play-in game, which Charlotte won in overtime thanks to Ball's last-second layup.

But for the Heat and their fans, it doesn't erase Adebayo's injury, it doesn't remove Ball from Friday's 8-9 game against the Orlando Magic and it all but certainly won't impact the Hornets should they reach the first round.

That's because one quirk of the tournament's addition is that, not unlike the NBA Cup title game, the play-in tournament lives as its own statistical entity. They are neither playoff nor regular-season games, with no bearing on postseason and regular-season stats or awards.

That's also the case with flagrant foul points, which can have a massive impact when they start to add up. In 2016, Draymond Green was suspended for Game 5 of the NBA Finals for accumulating four flagrant points over the course of the postseason, something that helped Cleveland pull off its stunning 3-1 comeback.

While the Hornets' playoff stay isn't likely to last as long -- Charlotte needs to win Friday just to set up a first-round meeting with the top-seeded Detroit Pistons -- Ball entering the playoffs with two flagrant points would have at least given heft to the belated punishment.

Instead, the decision felt fairly hollow. And in asking sources around the league Wednesday ahead of the NBA's announcement that Ball wouldn't be suspended, opinions were mixed. Some argued that a hefty fine would suffice, because you shouldn't retroactively remove him from the next game because of Adebayo's unfortunate injury. Others argued the opposite, saying he should have to sit out Friday's win-and-in showdown.

None of it, however, will reverse the agonizing end to Miami's season.

"I'm not really thinking about that anymore," Heat coach Erik Spoelstra told reporters Thursday during the team's exit interviews. "I don't think [Ball] is a dirty player. It should have been caught in the moment, and it wasn't. And you move on." -- Tim Bontemps

The NBA's take on tanking

ESPN's Anthony Slater talked to players, coaches and executives about how they feel about tanking in the NBA and the future it has in the league.

In ESPN's conversations with dozens of players, coaches and front office executives, a consistent theme emerged: Nobody likes it -- "I hate it," Golden State Warriors coach Steve Kerr said -- but not many deny it is often the most prudent team-building path when stuck near the bottom. Different seasons and different drafts will generate different forms, but everyone agrees it'll continue until the NBA figures out either the proper rules or punishments to curb it.

"These teams are doing the whole gamut: sitting guys in the fourth, playing analytically bad lineups, drawing up plays for bad shots," one Western Conference general manager said. stories.headline: QB Sam Darnold back Sunday, but Seahawks down two safeties
stories.summary: Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will start Sunday, but the defending Super Bowl champions will be without both starting safeties as Julian Love and Ty Okada have been ruled out.
stories.body:
RENTON, Wash. -- Seattle Seahawks quarterback Sam Darnold will start Sunday against the Washington Commanders, but the defending Super Bowl champions will be without both starting safeties as Julian Love and Ty Okada have been ruled out.

Backup defensive tackle Brandon Pili (concussion/neck) is questionable. No other Seahawks player has a game designation.

Darnold missed most of the first two games with a glute injury he suffered early in the season opener. He was limited Wednesday in his return to practice and was a full participant Thursday and Friday. Coach Mike Macdonald said Friday that Darnold looked "really good" this week.

"Sam's going to play, and he's ready to go," Macdonald said. "He's done a great job."

Speaking with reporters Thursday, Darnold said he briefly feared that his season might be over -- and that his career could be impacted long term -- when he was hurt on the fifth play of Seattle's Week 1 win over the New England Patriots. After backup Drew Lock led Seattle to a 31-7 win over the Arizona Cardinals and a 2-0 start last week, Macdonald said Darnold's timetable had "shifted quite drastically" for the better.

Macdonald was asked Friday what he needed to see from Darnold this week.

"Really just to see him confident in the things that he's been doing," Macdonald said. "He's been really positive and says he feels great. He looks great, so we'll rolling. It's a medical miracle he's back."

Rodney Thomas II will make his third straight start for Okada, who remains out with a hamstring injury. Macdonald said AJ Finley will start for Love, who popped up on the injury report as a nonparticipant Thursday when a calf tightened up. Love was again a nonparticipant Friday. Macdonald said he doesn't know how much time Love will miss.

Love has an interception in three straight games dating to Seattle's Super Bowl LX win over New England.

Finley will make his first start since entering the NFL as an undrafted free agent out of Mississippi in 2023. Claimed off waivers from the Los Angeles Chargers in November 2024, Finley missed all of last season after tearing an ACL in the team's annual training camp practice at Lumen Field. After intercepting Darnold during the same event this summer, Finley acknowledged how meaningful it was to him, calling it a "full-circle moment."

"You're really bummed about Julian obviously because he's had such a great start to the season and he's such a great player," Macdonald said. "But when AJ got the pick in training camp, I'm thinking about the journey he's been on over the last year and the way he's really gotten his body back and his movement. He had a great practice today. He's on it. He's sharp as a whip, great communication, ball skills, all those things. So I'm excited for him to have the opportunity."

Okada is still unable to practice.

"It's just a day-to-day to week-to-week type of thing," Macdonald said. "So for him to come back ... he's got to start making a little more progress. But he's a stud, he's working his tail off."

Nick Emmanwori, who plays extensively in the box as Seattle's third safety, was a full participant for the third straight day. Macdonald said this week that Emmanwori is in line for a significantly larger workload than the nine snaps he got last week in his return from July ankle surgery.

Rookie running back Jadarian Price, who started the first two games, progressed to full participation Friday after a chest/shoulder injury limited him Wednesday and Thursday.

"He's taken a ton of reps," Macdonald said. "Excited to see him to go play. He's ready to go."

Running back Zach Charbonnet -- Seattle's co-starter last season -- has to miss at least two more games while on the physically unable to perform list. The Seahawks did not open his 21-day practice window this week. Macdonald said Friday that they might do so next week.

stories.headline: Mauricio Pochettino: Cavan Sullivan ready for USMNT debut
stories.summary: USMNT coach Mauricio Pochettino said 16-year-old phenom Cavan Sullivan is ready to play for the USMNT during the current international window, but was non-committal as to what role he would play in Saturday's friendly against Peru.
stories.body:
ORLANDO -- United States men's national team coach Mauricio Pochettino said 16-year-old phenom Cavan Sullivan is ready to play for the USMNT during the current international window, but was noncommittal as to what role he would play in Saturday's friendly against Peru.

Sullivan has garnered the most attention on the current squad, even as 13 players that were part of the World Cup are also on the current roster.

This is due not only to his age, but also his recent performances for the Philadelphia Union, which have seen him score six goals and add eight assists in his last eight league games.

That has led to a tidal wave of anticipation to see what Sullivan can do at international level. If he plays, he'll be the youngest player since Freddy Adu to suit up for the USMNT.

Pochettino said earlier this month that he and the staff needed to be "careful" in how they manager the young attacker. He was circumspect in his assessment of Sullivan at Friday's pre-match news conference.

"If we only talk about his performance, he's doing really well in his club in Philadelphia. Talking only about that, I think he's ready, but the rest of the players too," Pochettino said about Sullivan. "He's mature enough on the field."

Pochettino also praised the entire group for how they performed in training this week, and lauded the vitality that the youngsters have brought to the group.

"They have talent, and they are showing the real talent," Pochettino said of the young players. "They have an amazing capacity and quality. And then the energy was amazing. It's very contagious, that energy."

Pochettino added that he will use a mix of youth and experience against Peru, and he'll take the data from training to determine who is ready to play and who isn't.

"When we observe the player, maybe some players need more time, maybe not to play the first game or the second, maybe the third or maybe some player training with us is enough and maybe they don't need to go to play," Pochettino said. "I think it's so important to provide the chance if they are ready."

The USMNT manager said he'll be looking at a variety of other factors as well in terms of deciding what constitutes "ready."

He indicated he's been spending much of the week getting to know the players off the field as well as on. He's observed how the new players adapt to the environment, especially when the staff sets the tone early.

"I think if the young kids arrive in an environment that they smell respect, they smell the discipline, the normal discipline in a team that plays soccer, I think they are very natural," he said.

"I think what we need to, that was our plan is to create an environment that they can feel natural. We want them to behave in a natural way because they are intelligent, they're smart and they perceive and feel in the way that they need to act when they arrive."

Pochettino's assessment included getting the young players to get up on stage at a team dinner, one at a time, and sing a song in front of the team and staff.

"In all these types of things, you start to see their personality, their character, capacity to move," Pochettino said. "And then when they start to train, how the senior players respect them and start to play together and see how they move, how they talk, how they communicate, that's key. Then of course you need to talk with them and say, you feel that you are ready or not? But I think it's good to ask them, but at the same time it's to perceive and to read all this type of situation to be sure that they can go."

stories.headline: Max Verstappen labels Azerbaijan GP qualifying a 'disaster,' starts eighth
stories.summary: Max Verstappen saw Red Bull's encouraging pace disappear in a "disaster" qualifying in Baku, where he will start from eighth on the grid for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.
stories.body:
Max Verstappen saw Red Bull's encouraging pace disappear in a "disaster" qualifying in Baku, where he will start from eighth on the grid for the Azerbaijan Grand Prix.

Verstappen had gone quickest in final practice Friday but was unable to contend in qualifying, ending Q3 in eighth place, 1.5 seconds off pole sitter George Russell.

Verstappen's teammate, Isack Hadjar, qualified fourth, 0.6 seconds quicker than the four-time world champion.

Russell was in a league of his own at the front and looks like strong favorite for victory, but Verstappen will start Saturday's race with two Ferraris, two McLarens, the other Red Bull and Pierre Gasly's Alpine in front of him.

When asked where he might be able to fight back to, Verstappen told Sky Sports: "I have no idea. We were in a really good place the whole weekend, and we had a disaster of a qualifying because of a lot of issues. Let's see tomorrow what we can do."

In the final seconds of qualifying, Lando Norris had gone off, prompting yellow flags around the part of the track where Verstappen was.

The Red Bull driver refused to blame that, saying the pace from practice just disappeared from the moment qualifying started.

"I mean [the yellow flags were] the last thing that happened," Verstappen said. "The whole qualifying I was just lacking top speed, half a second a lap off just on top speed, even compared to my teammate. The engine was just not working. So, that's one problem.

- Mercedes' George Russell takes thrilling pole for Azerbaijan Grand Prix

- Kimi Antonelli hits wall and suffers early exit from Azerbaijan Grand Prix qualifying

- George Russell 'shocked' by Azerbaijan GP pole: 'The biggest margin in my whole career'

"Then in Q3, in my middle lap," he said, "I tried to start and the battery didn't charge, so you start the lap with half a battery, so you have to abort. Then you lose temperature because you don't have enough power.

"That then snowballs into the final lap. I started the lap, but no top speed, a yellow flag in my lap, not enough tire temperature, and then that's where you are."

Verstappen has a spotty qualifying record at Baku's circuit. Friday was the fifth time he has been outqualified by a teammate there, the most of any other venue on the calendar.

Isaac Heeney is on track to be crowned the Sydney Swans' club champion after the AFL club ruled out changing the eligibility criteria for its best-and-fairest award.

But midfielder Heeney won't attend the awards night next week, requesting to skip the event along with Chad Warner, Nick Blakey, James Jordon and Riley Bice.

The five served a club-imposed ban from August, including the Swans' finals campaign, for breaching club standards following a post-AFL match party at the Pullman Hotel in East Melbourne.

Heeney and fellow ball-winner Warner are the frontrunners -- ahead of ruck Brodie Grundy -- for the club's Bob Skilton Medal, which will be presented at Sydney Town Hall next Thursday.

The club confirmed on Friday that eligibility and voting criteria will remain unchanged, leaving all players who represented the Swans this season eligible to win the award.

Heeney has won the club's last two best-and-fairest awards, while Warner finished runner-up to Callum Mills in 2022.

The AFL also opted against ruling out Heeney and Warner for the Brownlow Medal, but did not invite the pair to last Monday night's awards dinner at Crown Palladium.

The five players were made ineligible for All-Australian honours.

It comes after the five earlier this week returned to Swans headquarters for the first time since August, individually offering apologies to colleagues and teammates.

Heeney was the only player after the club meeting to address media on Wednesday, doing so with a brief statement.

"It was really nice to address the whole club," he said on Wednesday evening.

"Extremely thankful they could give us their time and understanding, so yeah, it was really good."

Warner spoke upon arriving at headquarters and said he was "just here for my exit interview".

Their club-imposed suspensions are separate from a police investigation into sexual assault allegations.

No charges have been laid, and AAP is not suggesting any wrongdoing on the part of the suspended players. Bice was subsequently cleared by police.

All five are contracted for next year, with Blakey signed to the club until 2031.

Warner and Jordon come off contract at the end of 2027, while Heeney and Bice are signed until the end of 2028.

Blakey is reportedly seeking a trade to Victorian rivals, but football boss Leon Cameron had dismissed those rumblings as "speculation" earlier this month.

Victoria Police's eight-week timeline prediction on their investigation into the Pullman Hotel incident -- which was first flagged on September 2 -- takes in the free agency and trade period from October 2 to October 14.

stories.headline: The performance bonuses for Van, Tsarukyan? Spots in P4P top 10
stories.summary: Former UFC champion puts elite status of women's flyweight division on display in ESPN's P4P top 10.
stories.body:
UFC 331 delivered some remarkable performances, a couple of which landed fighters in the ESPN pound-for-pound rankings.

One of them is not heavyweight Sean Sharaf, despite him pulling off the biggest upset in UFC history with his 12-second knockout of mega-prospect Gable Steveson. Women's flyweight Casey O'Neill produced a leading candidate for submission of the year, escaping a dangerous position to quickly armbar Eduarda Moura, but that didn't earn O'Neill a top-10 spot, either.

Both of those fighters were eye openers, but the rankings were reserved for the two winners of Saturday's headline fights.

In the main event, Joshua Van successfully defended his men's flyweight title against former champion Alexandre Pantoja, using crisp boxing and efficient grappling to secure a unanimous decision. Van moves into the men's rankings at No. 8, and Pantoja, who previously occupied that position, drops out.

Also earning a top-10 spot is co-main event winner Arman Tsarukyan, who knocked out flashy striker Mauricio Ruffy to all but secure a lightweight title shot. Tsarukyan moves in at No. 10, with former light heavyweight champion Alex Pereira falling from the rankings.

For the ESPN divisional MMA rankings, click here.

Note: Results are current; rankings are as of Sept. 23. To be eligible for the rankings, a fighter must have competed over the past 12 months or must have an upcoming fight booked. Fighters who have been dropped for inactivity can be reinstated only after they compete.

Men's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Islam Makhachev

UFC welterweight champion

Record: 29-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Ian Machado Garry, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Makhachev vacated the UFC lightweight championship to go for a second title at welterweight. By winning that belt last November with a thrashing of Jack Della Maddalena, Makhachev staked his place among MMA's greatest -- not just in today's sport but of all time. His win over Machado Garry at UFC 330 was his 17th straight, breaking the UFC record for consecutive wins. Makhachev is piling up unprecedented achievements.

2. Petr Yan

UFC bantamweight champion

Record: 20-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Merab Dvalishvili, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Dvalishvili

What a return to the top it's been for Yan. He began his career with 15 consecutive wins before going on a 1-4 run from 2021 to 2023. That almost doesn't feel real now, after watching him reclaim his throne against Dvalishvili, who once handed him the worst loss of his career. Yan took a major detour, but this was the destination we felt he was capable of before the skid. He once again looks like one of the best fighters on the planet. He can prove it by beating Dvalishvili again.

3. Merab Dvalishvili

UFC bantamweight

Record: 21-5

Last: L (UD) vs. Petr Yan, Dec. 6, 2025

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Yan

Dvalishvili was on one of the most impressive runs through the UFC's bantamweight division ever. Not only did he defeat Sean O'Malley for the second time in nine months at UFC 316, but he showcased a new part of his game, finishing O'Malley with a guillotine. Starting in August 2022, Dvalishvili beat José Aldo, Yan, Henry Cejudo, O'Malley (twice), Umar Nurmagomedov and Cory Sandhagen. But at UFC 323, in an attempt to become the first champion in UFC history to successfully defend a title four times in a calendar year, Dvalishvili lost a rematch with Yan. They will fight for a third time at UFC 333.

T-4. Tom Aspinall

UFC heavyweight

Record: 15-3, 1 NC

Last: NC1 vs. Ciryl Gane, Oct. 25, 2025

Next: TBA

You can make a case that Aspinall is the most dynamic, skillful, talented heavyweight the sport has seen. He is dominating opponents in a way that is unmatched. No one can last a round with him. He had hoped to prove his supremacy against Jon Jones, but Jones opted to retire, elevating Aspinall from interim champion. His first defense of the undisputed belt ended anticlimactically, as an eye poke resulted in his UFC 321 fight with Gane being declared a no-contest. Still recovering from the eye injury, Aspinall vacated his title on Sept. 14.

T-4. Justin Gaethje

UFC lightweight champion

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 28-5

Last: W (TKO4) vs. Ilia Topuria, June 14

Next: TBA

Gaethje has spent his 15-year career thrilling MMA fans, but before the title bout on the White House lawn, all he had to show for it -- aside from 15 bonus checks in 15 UFC appearances -- were two missed opportunities to be an undisputed champion. His fourth-round TKO of Topuria got Gaethje over the hump. It was a resilient performance in a back-and-forth battle that is a prime candidate for fight of the year. More important for Gaethje: At age 37, he is finally sitting at the top of the mountain.

6. Ilia Topuria

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: 5

Record: 17-1

Last: L (TKO4) vs. Justin Gaethje, June 14

Next: TBA

Topuria was an undefeated two-division champion when he ran into Gaethje at UFC Freedom 250 and was brutalized in a stoppage loss. How will that affect the immediate future of Topuria? His knockout wins over two of the greatest featherweights, Alexander Volkanovski and Max Holloway, gave him an intimidating aura. Can the former champion get that back?

7. Alexander Volkanovski

UFC featherweight champion

Record: 28-4

Last: W (UD) vs. Diego Lopes, Jan. 31

Next: Oct. 24 vs. Movsar Evloev

It felt as if the sport had started to write Volkanovski's eulogy following his knockout loss to Ilia Topuria in February 2024. Volkanovski noticed and made a point of proving to everyone he still has plenty left by recapturing the featherweight belt at UFC 314, the first of two consecutive wins over Lopes. His age (37) will likely continue to be a prefight topic, which is fine because Volkanovski enjoys proving people wrong. Can he hand Evloev his first loss at UFC 333?

8. Joshua Van

UFC flyweight champion

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 18-2

Last: W (UD) vs. Alexandre Pantoja, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Van has been champion since December, but until UFC 331, there were doubters. Van had been handed the belt by default, when his challenge for the title was waved off after 26 seconds because Pantoja dislocated his left elbow. Van went on to defend the title against Tatsuro Taira in May, then faced Pantoja in a rematch this past weekend. Van produced a clear victory -- his eighth win in a row -- to leave no doubt who rules at 125 pounds.

9. Ciryl Gane

UFC heavyweight champion

Record: 14-2, 1 NC

Last: W (TKO2) vs. Alex Pereira, June 14

Next: Nov. 14 vs. Josh Hokit

Gane is unique in that he is the first -- and could very well go down as the only -- heavyweight to face the division's four biggest names in Francis Ngannou, Jon Jones, Tom Aspinall and Pereira. None of those four have fought each other, yet all four have have fought the Frenchman. Gane was 0-2 with a no-contest against that group before he knocked out Pereira in the second round of their interim title fight. Gane was elevated to undisputed champ after Aspinall, still injured, vacated his title, and the new champ will defend against Hokit at UFC 334.

10. Arman Tsarukyan

UFC lightweight

Previous ranking: Unranked

Record: 24-3

Last: W (KO1) vs. Mauricio Ruffy, Sept. 19

Next: TBA

Tsarukyan is right back in the place he was in January 2025 -- on the cusp of a title fight. He withdrew from that challenge of Islam Makhachev one day before UFC 311 because of a back injury, and later in the year he was passed over twice when the UFC was booking lightweight title bouts. But by knocking out Mauricio Ruffy with an elbow in the first round at UFC 331, Tsarukyan put himself back at the front of the line.

Other fighter receiving votes: Alex Pereira.

How our panel voted

Women's pound-for-pound rankings

1. Valentina Shevchenko

UFC flyweight

Record: 26-4-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Zhang Weili, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

Shevchenko's dominance came under question in 2022 and 2023, when she went 1-1-1 in a trilogy with Alexa Grasso. Boy, does that feel like a long time ago now. Shevchenko more than reasserted herself as the best flyweight in the world, and then she established herself as the No. 1 woman in the world, period. It wasn't surprising that she beat Zhang, but it was surprising how easy she made it look. Shevchenko is out injured, however, so she has vacated her UFC title, which will be up for grabs when Natalia Silva meets Wang Cong on Oct. 3.

2. Zhang Weili

UFC flyweight / strawweight

Record: 26-4

Last: L (UD) vs. Valentina Shevchenko, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: TBA

It's hard to move up in weight, especially at the highest level. That sounds like it should be obvious, but Zhang had been dominant at 115 pounds for so long, some of us might have taken for granted how big of a challenge moving to 125 would be. UFC 322 was a bad night for Zhang, but she doesn't have many. And if she decides to stay at flyweight, it certainly seems reasonable to believe she'll fare better in the future.

3. Cris Cyborg

PFL featherweight champion

Record: 30-2, 1 NC

Last: W (UD) vs. Ketlen Vieira, Aug. 22

Next: TBA

It had been a while since Cyborg had fought an elite opponent in MMA until she met Larissa Pacheco in 2024. That was a legitimate matchup -- and many within the industry were predicting Cyborg's downfall. Instead, she took out the PFL's two-weight champion, upending all of Pacheco's momentum. One of the original pioneers of women's MMA is once again a champion after getting her second career submission at PFL Lyon in December. The PFL promoted her fight with Vieira as a retirement bout, but after her win Cyborg did not sound like someone who is done fighting.

4. Mackenzie Dern

UFC strawweight champion

Record: 17-5

Last: W (UD) vs. Gillian Robertson, Aug. 15

Next: TBA

Dern's rise to the 115-pound throne was truly a changing of the guard. She is the division's first first-time champion since 2019, because the previous three champs -- Zhang Weili, Carla Esparza and Rose Namajunas -- all were in their second reigns. Dern, nearly a decade into her MMA career after multiple jiu-jitsu world championships, has won four fights in a row, including a dominant performance against a fellow grappling-heavy fighter, Robertson, in her first title defense.

5. Natalia Silva

UFC flyweight

Record: 20-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Rose Namajunas, Jan. 24

Next: Oct. 3 vs. Wang Cong

Silva is looking every bit the part of a future UFC champion following a dominant display against Alexa Grasso at UFC 315 and a victory over Namajunas at UFC 324. Silva's stick-and-move style has frustrated even the highest level of opponent, and she's got youth on her side as she won't turn 30 until 2027. With an injured Valentina Shevchenko having vacated the title, Silva will fight Wang for the belt at UFC 332.

6. Alexa Grasso

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 10

Record: 18-5-1

Last: W (UD) vs. Manon Fiorot, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Grasso went nearly three years without winning a fight, but her 2023 win right before the skid was a huge one, a submission of Valentina Shevchenko for the UFC title. What followed were two more fights with Shevchenko -- a draw, then a loss -- and then a loss to Natalia Silva. But she reasserted herself with a finish of Maycee Barber in March, then got the best of Fiorot, a fellow title contender, at Noche UFC to put herself in position for another title shot.

7. Dakota Ditcheva

PFL flyweight

Record: 16-0

Last: W (UD) vs. Denise Kielholtz, July 31

Next: TBA

Not only did Ditcheva win the PFL's flyweight season in 2024, but she did so in spectacular fashion -- a TKO finish over Taila Santos, who once challenged for a UFC title. Ditcheva fought only once in 2025, dominating Sumiko Inaba in the co-main event of the first PFL Champions Series card in Cape Town, South Africa. She then spent over a year on the sideline, healing injuries to both hands, before returning at PFL New York with a dominant win over Kielholtz.

8. Manon Fiorot

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 6

Record: 13-3

Last: L (UD) vs. Alexa Grasso, Sept. 12

Next: TBA

Fiorot had handled everyone the UFC put in front of her -- except the champion, Valentina Shevchenko, who defeated the Frenchwoman at UFC 315 in May 2025. But then, with another title shot within her grasp, Fiorot ran into Grasso, a former champion, at Noche UFC and lost a competitive fight.

9. Erin Blanchfield

UFC flyweight

Previous ranking: 8

Record: 14-2

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Tracy Cortez, Nov. 15, 2025

Next: Oct. 17 vs. Jasmine Jasudavicius

Her rise toward the top of the division was derailed by a March 2024 loss to Manon Fiorot, but Blanchfield bounced back with two straight wins, including one over two-time former strawweight champion Rose Namajunas in November 2024. If she wins her October bout with Jasudavicius, a fellow top-10 flyweight contender, Blanchfield would inch ever closer to a title shot.

10. Tatiana Suarez

UFC strawweight

Previous ranking: 9

Record: 12-1

Last: W (Sub2) vs. Loopy Godínez, April 11

Next: TBA

If Suarez is still feeling the effects of last year's humbling defeat to Zhang Weili in a title challenge, she certainly didn't show it at UFC 327, overcoming early adversity to thrash Godinez, a fellow top-10 strawweight. Suarez is going to be a tough out for anyone at 115 pounds.

stories.headline: Still at zero: Viral Man United fan's haircut challenge nears two years
stories.summary: Viral Manchester United fan Frank Ilett's haircut challenge is nearing the two-year mark and he's back to square 1.
stories.body:
For most clubs, failure or success can be defined in points, trophies and medals. Manchester United are the same, but they can also define it in days. More specifically, it can be summed up in 712 days.

That's how long viral United fan Frank Ilett, also known as The United Strand, has gone without a haircut as he waits for the team to win five games in a row.

After finishing last season with wins over Nottingham Forest and Brighton, Michael Carrick's side could have completed the job with wins over newly promoted Hull City and Ipswich Town before finishing with a win away at Everton. As it turned out, that's not at all what happened.

An embarrassing 2-0 away defeat to Hull meant going back to square one. A 5-2 win over Ipswich might have promoted hopes that the season opener was just an unwanted blip, but a draw to Everton and a controversial defeat to 10-man Manchester City poured further cold water.

How could it get worse? Well, a 2-0 lead inside the first 10 minutes against Brighton in the Carabao Cup ended in a surprise 3-2 defeat.

Left watching on, his hair growing ever longer, is Ilett. His challenge will now officially reach the two-year mark -- his last haircut was on Oct. 5, 2024 -- and his hair is now almost 14 inches at its longest point.

In the meantime, Ilett continues to raise money for the Little Princess Trust, which creates wigs for children with cancer.

The only thing that can happen now before Ilett soars past two years is for United to win away to Fulham in their last game before the international break.

stories.headline: Victor Radley cleared, Roosters sweating on Connor Watson
stories.summary: Victor Radley has learnt his grand final fate after a hip-drop tackle, while Connor Watson is hoping to be cleared to play for the Sydney Roosters.
stories.body:
Connor Watson could still feature in the NRL grand final for the Sydney Roosters, with the Tri-colours set to kick off the process of clearing concussion protocols for the decider.

The Roosters were breathing a sigh of relief on Saturday morning, with Victor Radley avoiding a suspension for his hip-drop tackle on Herbie Farnworth in the 36-20 preliminary-final win over the Dolphins.

Radley can enter an early guilty plea and pay a $2000 fine, which would clear him to play in next Sunday's decider against Penrith or Newcastle.

But the bigger headache for the Roosters may be Watson.

The super sub had been on the field for just 60 seconds when his head collided with Dolphins forward Kulikefu Finefeuiaki's hip in the 31st minute at Suncorp Stadium on Friday.

The knock was originally ruled as a category two by the Roosters, before that was overruled by the independent doctor, who deemed it a category one.

That ruled Watson out of the game and triggered an 11-day stand-down that would keep him out of next Sunday's decider in Sydney.

But Trent Robinson said post-game Watson was undergoing more tests, with the coach refusing to rule out seeking an exemption for the NSW Origin utility.

"That was a hard one; he came out as a category two, they changed it to a one after a couple of minutes," Robinson said.

"That's still 'watch this space' on Connor. It depends on how his tests go (if the Roosters appeal), so we'll see how that goes."

Watson is the first player at risk of missing an NRL grand final under the 11-day stand-down run, which was introduced in 2023.

Penrith had faced the potential of a similar situation last year, when Scott Sorensen suffered a head knock in their preliminary final loss to Brisbane.

Sorensen was also deemed to be a category two by club medical staff, before the NRL's independent doctor classed it as a category one.

Had Penrith won the match, it is understood they would have appealed to have Sorensen play in the grand final.

There have been multiple instances this year of players challenging category one concussions and being able to play the next week.

However Watson would still need to prove he was wrongly classified and be asymptomatic from Saturday morning, among several other requirements.

In more positive news for the Roosters, Sam Walker emerged unscathed after a record-equalling 27-day comeback from a syndesmosis injury.

The halfback left the field early with the match decided, but not before delivering a masterclass in orchestrating his backline.

The Roosters have not lost a grand final under Robinson, who will now be angling for his fourth premiership as a coach in the club's first decider since 2019.

"It's mostly internal, you want to get the most out of it," he said of the pressure to return to the big stage.

"I know what my role is ... it's not about getting into a grand final, it's about winning it.

"That's pretty simple and that's what I'm here to do."

stories.headline: Sources: Warriors, Curry reach 2-year extension worth $116 million
stories.summary: Warriors star Stephen Curry agreed to a two-year, $116 million contract extension, sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Friday, ultimately opting for a pay cut and security over a max contract.
stories.body:
Golden State Warriors star Stephen Curry has agreed to a two-year, $116 million contract extension, tying the franchise legend to the only organization he has ever known through his 20th NBA season, league sources told ESPN's Shams Charania on Friday.

The deal includes a player option in the final season (2028-29), according to sources.

The Warriors presented Curry with several contract choices in recent weeks, including the option to wait, but Curry ultimately decided on a pay cut and security over either a max contract or the uncertainty of stalling for more flexibility and information.

Curry is currently on an expiring $62.6 million contract and became eligible Aug. 29 for an extension for up to two years and $136.7 million.

As part of the Warriors' presentation to Curry, the team laid out various paths that included the idea of a slight pay cut from his max, delivering them more salary cap room to build a contender around him in the future, team sources said.

Curry's contract will dip from $62.6 million next season to $55.7 million for the 2027-28 season and a player option for $60.2 million in the 2028-29 season. That will provide the Warriors with around $10 million extra in projected cap space next summer, allowing them to be a bigger player in either free agency or the trade market in the next 12 months.

Currently, Jimmy Butler III ($56.8 million) and Draymond Green ($27.6 million) both have expiring contracts coming off the Warriors' books next summer. Veteran center Kristaps Porzingis has only $3 million of his $20 million salary guaranteed, leaving the Warriors somewhere between $38 million and a projected $55 million in cap space, depending on what they do with Brandin Podziemski's extension eligibility, according to ESPN's Bobby Marks. Podziemski, who has yet to extend, has a $17 million cap hold next summer.

Curry took nearly a month to decide whether he wanted to sign for his full max, accept a slight pay cut or wait to agree to a new deal.

"We're in a very interesting situation," Curry told ESPN earlier this week. "All the different salary cap conditions of whether I sign for a max or less or whatever it is, I want to be on a competitive team. I want to have an opportunity to have some flexibility because we haven't had that in years past, the recent past. ... This team should have flexibility to make necessary moves if things happen. Those are always just the considerations.

"For me, information and patience is key. It's just a very unique situation all the way around based on where we've been the last four years, where I'm at in my career, what our team looks like this year and the absolute desperation to win. Trying to balance all that."

Curry, who said he wanted "no drama" surrounding his contract talks heading into training camp, opted for the pay cut and security three days before the team's first practice, quieting any lingering questions.

Curry, who turns 39 this season, missed 39 games because of a persistent right knee issue last season but said he felt great entering camp.

"The idea of getting back to work is exciting," Curry said. "I feel like I've taken advantage of the offseason. I feel like there's no hesitation about where I'm at physically going in. ... But I'm excited about getting back to work."

The extension brings Curry's career on-court earnings to $652 million, making him the first player to eclipse $600 million in NBA history.

stories.headline: Rangers falter in AL West chase, lose to Twins 10-2 as deGrom matches high by allowing 8 earned runs
stories.summary: — Jacob deGrom matched a career high by allowing eight earned runs on Friday and the Texas Rangers stumbled again in the AL West race with a 10-2 loss to the Minnesota Twins.
stories.body:
MINNEAPOLIS -- — Jacob deGrom matched a career high by allowing eight earned runs on Friday and the Texas Rangers stumbled again in the AL West race with a 10-2 loss to the Minnesota Twins.


Texas (79-81) began the night tied with Houston, which has the tiebreaker. The Astros played at the Athletics later Friday,


Given a 2-0 lead, deGrom (11-11) gave up six runs in the second inning and two more in the fourth. He allowed eight hits and three walks while striking out five over four innings. It's the fourth time deGrom has allowed eight earned runs in a game.


Luke Keaschall had four hits, including a double and a triple, and drove in three runs for the Twins. Kody Clemens went 3 for 4 and hit his team-leading 27th homer of the season in the sixth inning.


Twins starter Joe Ryan (7-10) allowed two runs and four hits with eight strikeouts over six innings.


Corey Seager hit an RBI single and Wyatt Langford a run-scoring grounder as Rangers took advantage of two hit batters in the first inning.


Royce Lewis hit a tying, two-run single in the second game, and Ryan Kreidler brought home the go-ahead run with a safety squeeze bunt that turned into a single when nobody covered first base. Keaschall tripled in two more runs before scoring on a deGrom wild pitch.


Texas designated hitter Josh Jung was hit by a pitch on his right hand. He stayed in the game and scored the Rangers' second run, then was replaced by a pinch hitter in the third inning.


Up next
Twins RHP Bailey Ober (7-6, 4.21 ERA) starts Saturday against a pitcher to be determined.

stories.body:
Manchester United are keeping tabs on Club Brugge left back Joaquin Seys, while Barcelona attacking midfielder Dani Olmo is on the radar of Bayern Munich. Join us for the latest transfer news and rumors from around the globe.

United scouts recently watched the 21-year-old provide two assists in a 3-0 win over Genk as they evaluate defensive cover for 31-year-old Luke Shaw, after missing out on primary summer targets Nathaniel Brown (who joined Bayern Munich) and Newcastle United's Lewis Hall (who signed a new contract.)

-Bayern Munich are lining up a January move for Barcelona attacking midfielder Dani Olmo, according to Sky Sports. The German giants are preparing contingency plans amid growing interest from rival clubs in Jamal Musiala and Michael Olise, and have maintained a long-term interest in the 28-year-old that dates back to his time at RB Leipzig. Olmo, who won the World Cup with Spain this summer, has a transfer valuation estimated at €70 million and could be offloaded as Barcelona look to build funds to sign Julián Álvarez from Atlético Madrid.

stories.headline: Embolo out of Switzerland squad over fake COVID-19 documents
stories.summary: World Cup quarterfinalist Switzerland has lost a second player from its Nations League squad because of years-old cases of fake COVID-19 documents.
stories.body:
BERN, Switzerland -- World Cup quarterfinalist Switzerland has lost a second player from its Nations League squad because of years-old cases of fake COVID-19 documents.

Breel Embolo will not join the squad in Scotland as planned, the Swiss soccer federation said Friday, due to fresh reporting in national media about his past case of obtaining forged test certificates in 2021.

- Embolo: People in Europe 'shocked' at MLS move

- Embolo debut goal gives Atlanta draw at Miami

"This decision aims to allow the team to remain fully focused on the next matches," the federation said about the Atlanta United forward.

Switzerland captain Granit Xhaka agreed with team officials last weekend to withdraw from the squad because he is implicated in an investigation of a doctor issuing fake vaccination certificates during the COVID-19 pandemic.

Xhaka, the Swiss record holder with 152 caps, admitted getting the forged document in 2022 and accepted he made mistakes.

Switzerland starts its Nations League second-tier group Saturday at North Macedonia, plays at Scotland on Tuesday, then has home games in Lucerne against Slovenia and North Macedonia.

Embolo already was suspended for the game Saturday because of his controversial red card against Argentina in the World Cup quarterfinals.

Soccer's Zurich-based rules panel, known as IFAB, later acknowledged Embolo was mistakenly sent off in a breach of video review protocol.

On Friday, the Switzerland Today outlet reported details of Embolo's financial sanction imposed last year for the previously known false test result documents.

At the World Cup, the 29-year-old Embolo scored in Switzerland's opening game -- a 1-1 draw with Qatar -- despite arriving at the tournament days later than teammates because of a visa issue with United States authorities. He also scored in a round of 32 win over Algeria.
